title: A map is an equivalence as soon as each point of its codomain supplies a proof that it is one
author: The Univalent Foundations Program
work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled corollary at source lines 481-483: if every point of the codomain supplies a proof that the map is an equivalence, then the map is an equivalence. The proof (source lines 484-487) is short but it is the reduction itself and not a pointer: it moves to the fibre criterion, fixes an arbitrary point of the codomain, applies the assumed map there to get a proof of equivalence at that point, and reads the contractibility of the homotopy fibre out of it. Which criterion licenses the reduction and where the hypothesis is consumed is the substance, and the statement alone does not display it.
